chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man from whom I bought food on credit for a specified term. When the term arrived, I took it from him with my dirhams. He said, 'I do not have dirhams, but I have food with me, so buy it from me.' He (the Imam) said, 'Do not buy it from him, for there is no good in it.'

This does not contradict the first report, because what the first report included regarding the permissibility of that is only permissible if he takes the food as it was sold to him, without increase or decrease. The prohibition in the second report applies to the one who takes the food more than what he had given, or less.

key_terms.لَا خَيْرَ فِيهِ: there is no good in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to settle a food debt with food of a different quantity or quality?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the distinction between permissible debt settlement and riba by noting that the prohibition applies when the creditor takes food of a different quantity or quality, whereas returning the exact same type and amount is valid. This resolves the apparent contradiction between earlier narrations allowing such transactions and this specific prohibition, emphasizing that the core issue is the potential for hidden usury through variation in the returned commodity.
